findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple containers of foods in the front walk in cooler were observed without lids and/or other coverings to protect them from miscellaneous contamination during storage. The PIC was shown and had staff add coverings or lids to all of the observed food items during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all stored foods are protected from contaminants while they are being stored.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet during the inspection. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees and provide sufficient oversight to ensure hand washing takes place correctly in the facility. Ensure that hands are not recontaminated at the end step of the hand washing process in the facility.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A container of beef was observed on the floor under shelving in the walk in cooler. A conversation took place with the PIC and the container was moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored so that possible contamination is prohibited.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Three locations have temperature violations observed at this time. 1) The drink prep cooler in the front section of the facility is holding milk at 51F. The PIC was shown and discarded the milk to correct. The cooler should either be turned down or (because it is the only TCS item in this cooler) the milk should be moved to another cooler moving forward. 2) The walk in cooler closest to the dish area is observed with items at 45-50 internal temperatures. These items (cheese, pork buns, mayonnaise and a dairy based sauce were all discarded during this inspection. 3) The other walk in cooler is observed with TCS foods that have internal temperatures between 44F-52F. There is some evidence that this cooler MAY be in a defrost cycle, (dripping ice blocks and thicker items having lower temperatures). Because of this, the TCS items in this cooler is being embargoed until safe temperatures can be verified. This was communicated to the PICs and they are aware of how to handle this situation. The PIC indicated that workers arrive at the facility between 9 and 9:30 am. The inspector will return in the morning to verify temperatures at that time. Prior to embargoing, the PIC indicated that their maintenance company had already been scheduled to come out tomorrow for issues noted at this facility by the PICs. A follow up is currently being scheduled for Monday.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The facility did not have verifiable information of employee’s responsibility to report foodborne illness symptoms and diagnosis. Multiple copies of the reporting agreements given by SCDPH are observed blank in the paperwork binder. The PIC is instructed to make copies and have all food handlers sign a copy prior to the follow up. 10 days lands on a Saturday, the follow-up will be conducted on the following Monday.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-opening) 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a gap observed at the bottom right corner of the back door. Repair the door to ensure that the gap is removed to prevent possible entrance of pests. Ensure that all outer openings of the facility seal.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple containers of foods in the walk in cooler are observed without lids or other coverings. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to maintain foods covered when not in use. Ensure that all foods have coverings moving forward.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

On arrival multiple moist rags are observed on the counters in the kitchen. Rags are being used for wiping of counters and equipment. Education was conducted and the rags moved to newly provided buckets with a quat based sanitizer to correct. Ensure that sani rags are stored between uses in a sanitizer solution.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival the facility indicated that they were using an alcohol based sanitizer for their front prep surfaces. They do not currently have a test strip for this chemical. It should not be used in the food areas without a test strip available. Education was conducted and the bottle changed for a bucket with a quat based sanitizer to correct.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival the facility did not have a sanitizer ready for use in the main part of the kitchen. A bucket with a quat based sanitizer was produced during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-opening) 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) Seal holes in walls with silicon caulking. 2) Floor cover for floor drain right of the dish machine. 3) Replace cracked light shield in dry storage.
